evidence: CDIAL 13734 strī means woman/wife. The unchanged Bengali consonant cluster identifies the learned Sanskrit word; Kalasha istrīźā is separately identified in the article as a modern compound with jāyā and needs both parts represented.
CDIAL 10383 mriyate explicitly gives Khowar bri- die in the addendum and brik in the main entry. These bri-/brī- stems match that direct comparison; the hyphen is stem notation.
CDIAL 6559.3 *dehila explicitly gives Nepali dailo door/threshold. Majhi and Bote dailo select this branch rather than the dehalī or dehula branches.

CDIAL 7 aṃsiya explicitly gives Nepali hã̄siyo, Bengali/Hindi hã̄siyā and Bihari hãsuā sickle, as well as Kumaoni ã̄sī scythe. The selected forms preserve these y-bearing, u-bearing and h-less variants; uncertain regional transmission remains open.

CDIAL 2817 karkaṭa explicitly gives Nepali kā̃kro and related kā̃kri cucumber. These kãkro/kãkra forms fit that named plant family; the article qualifies its deeper relation to karkaṭa crab and karkāru.
CDIAL 1728 utkuṇa explicitly gives Bengali ukun and Oriya ukuṇi louse, alongside the nasal uṅkuṇa variant. Majhi ukuni/ũkuni matches this louse family with source nasalization retained.

CDIAL 1348 āryaka explicitly gives Bhojpuri ājā grandfather, ājī grandmother and Oriya ajā maternal grandfather. These aja/aji/aje forms fit the documented kinship family; source relationship specificity is retained.
CDIAL 5539.8 *devva explicitly gives Nepali debre left. These dental-initial Majhi/Bote forms select section 8 rather than retroflex *ḍevva in section 5.
CDIAL 4999 chardi explicitly gives Nepali chād vomit. Majhi/Bote cʰad matches the noun in that article.
